reviews.decision_reason: select_demand keeps every corpus row because the threshold is demand_score >= 3, including weak/background-style records and fallback records. Under the strict market-demand criteria, the boundary does not distinguish well-supported demand from generic or low-evidence candidates before handing data to normalization. The final one-record output hides this over-selection downstream, so this unit is behaviorally risky but not directly the final truncation point.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, and outcomes support selected demand claims
generic keyword matches and unrelated candidates are not included as demand evidence

reviews.decision_reason: normalize truncates the retained selected demand to retained_df.head(len(index_window)) with index_window = [0], yielding only n06-r01. This drops other selected corpus records, including records that appear in the downstream capability set, so the output cannot support comparison of selected and complete runtime evidence or coverage of available capabilities. The inspected artifacts confirm the normalized handoff contains exactly one row, n06-r01.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: bounded normalized needs DataFrame preserving allowed corpus identifiers
missing or contradictory evidence remains visible

reviews.decision_reason: assemble_provenance performs missing-safe extraction from the normalized needs handoff and deterministically ranks the rows by demand_score and record_id. The one-row provenance output is a consequence of the already-truncated normalize input, not a defect localized in this boundary.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: assemble ranked source provenance with missing-safe field access and deterministic ordering
